key_insight: Execution-state capsules let on-device AI systems checkpoint and restore the full graph-bound execution state—not just KV cache—so interactive agents can resume, branch, or roll back with very low latency.
engineering_relevance: This enables latency-first serving for robots, speech, and embedded LLM agents where responsiveness and correctness matter more than high-throughput batch reuse.
method: Capture the complete committed execution state as a graph-bound capsule over static contiguous buffers.
Restore, fork, or roll back all restorable state including KV, recurrent, convolution, MTP, and metadata.
Run captured graph plans on a CUDA backend without block-table indirection for deterministic replay.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports byte-exact restore, token-identical greedy decoding, sub-millisecond GPU-resident snapshot/restore, and TTFT speedups from 3.9x at 2k tokens to 27x at 16k tokens, validated on RTX 5090, Jetson AGX Thor, and DGX Spark.
watch_item: This approach depends on a closed set of named buffers and backend support for captured graph execution, so integration may be nontrivial for dynamic or highly custom model stacks.
paper_title: Execution-State Capsules: Graph-Bound Execution-State Checkpoint and Restore for Low-Latency, Small-Batch, On-Device Physical-AI Serving
